title: refactor(ci): consolidate CI workflows, upgrade Node to 18, and add release automation
author: Elena M. Ruiz
description: Consolidate multiple GitHub Actions workflows into a smaller set of reusable workflows, upgrade Node.js used in CI containers to 18, and introduce a guarded release automation workflow using semantic-release. Motivation: reduce CI maintenance overhead, improve PR feedback times by enabling targeted and cached jobs, fix flakes caused by mixed Node versions across jobs, and provide a safe automated release path for packages in the monorepo. The refactor moves shared steps into reusable workflows and actions, centralizes cache/key logic, introduces a deterministic matrix for package testing, and splits lint/test/build into focused pipelines so flaky or expensive jobs run only when relevant. The release workflow is added as a guarded, opt-in job (disabled by default) and performs a dry-run by default to validate changelog and versioning behavior. Behavioral changes are minimal and gated; no runtime application changes. See commits and changed files for details.

checks_summary: build-linux (ubuntu-latest) — pass (6m 12s); lint-fast — pass (45s); unit-tests (matrix: node18, node18-alpine, node18-buster) — pass (avg 5m 10s); integration-tests — pass (12m 8s); security-scan — pass; release (dry-run) — pass; total median PR feedback: ~7m
review_conversation:
Priya Nair: Please make sure node 18 is used consistently in all matrix entries and Dockerfiles — I saw node 16 in one of the ci images.
Elena M. Ruiz: Good catch — updated scripts/ci-dockerfile and package.json engines to 18, adjusted matrix config accordingly.
Diego Morales: Can we gate the release job behind an org secret and make dry-run the default? I don't want accidental publishes.
Elena M. Ruiz: Release job is disabled by default and requires RELEASE_TOKEN secret plus the 'release/enable' repo-level flag. Dry-run is the default; publishing requires manual toggle and a Linear approval step.
Avery Cooper: Verified caches and reusable workflows locally; lint job is much faster. Approving once CI passes.
Priya Nair: Left a small optional suggestion to log cache hit/miss metrics to console for first-week telemetry.
Elena M. Ruiz: Added cache logging and a brief doc entry in docs/ci.md. Thanks all for the review — addressing remaining nits now.
release_notes:
- Consolidated CI workflows into reusable templates under .github/workflows/reusable
- Upgraded CI Node runtime to Node.js v18 across all workflows and Docker images
- Added a guarded semantic-release workflow (dry-run by default, publishing disabled without explicit flag and secret)
- Centralized cache key logic to reduce cache misses and speed up PRs
- Split lint and formatting into a fast pre-check workflow to provide quicker feedback
- Updated docs/ci.md with local emulation instructions and rollout guidance
